Few television creators are as prolific as Taylor Sheridan.

Perhaps the most misunderstood creative in Hollywood, Sheridan has built a massive TV empire, beginning with his hit Western drama Yellowstone in 2018. The series, which ran on Paramount until 2025, starred Kevin Costner as John Dutton, a father and sixth-generation homesteader, who controls the country’s largest contiguous ranch.

The show has since spawned multiple prequels and spin-offs, including 1883, 1923 and Dutton Ranch. Sheridan recently revealed that the latest spin-off, 6666, has been permanently shelved, despite Paramount having announced it was in development.

Still, the king of Paramount remains booked and busy, with seven shows currently airing, and at least two more on the way.

Here is a rundown of all of Sheridan’s shows — past, present and forthcoming — that he has either created or that are based on characters he created.

open image in gallery Taylor Sheridan revealed that he never intended to make '6666,' despite Paramount previously announcing it was in development ( Getty )

Currently airing

Mayor of Kingstown (2021-)

open image in gallery Jeremy Renner leads ‘Mayor of Kingstown’ ( Dennis P. Mong Jr./Paramount+ )

Sheridan first stepped out of the Yellowstone universe with Mayor of Kingstown. The thriller — which follows the McKlusky family, who act as unofficial power brokers in their town of Kingston, Michigan, where incarceration is the only thriving industry — is expected to return to screens for its fifth and final season this fall.

It stars Jeremy Renner, who returned as Mike McKlusky in 2024 following his near-fatal snowplow accident.

Tulsa King (2022-)

open image in gallery ‘Tulsa King,’ starring Sylvester Stallone, has been renewed for a fourth season ( Frank Ockenfels/Paramount+ )

Following the overwhelming success of Mayor of Kingstown, Sheridan continued to expand his reach with the gritty mafia crime drama Tulsa King. The show centers on Dwight (Sylvester Stallone), a mob boss recently freed from prison and exiled to Oklahoma to set up shop. It marks the Rocky actor’s first-ever starring role in a scripted television series.

It has been renewed for a fourth season, with production wrapping in March. A premiere date has yet to be announced.

Lioness (2023-)

open image in gallery Zoe Saldana and Nicole Kidman co-star in 'Lioness' ( Paramount+ )

Currently in its third season, Lioness is a thriller featuring Zoe Saldaña and Nicole Kidman as CIA operatives balancing their personal and professional lives while leading the agency’s war on terror.

New episodes premiere Sundays on Paramount+.

Landman (2024-)

open image in gallery Billy Bob Thornton as crisis executive Tommy Norris in ‘Landman’ ( Paramount+ )

Landman, featuring an ensemble cast of Billy Bob Thornton, Demi Moore, Ali Larter, Sam Elliott, Michelle Randolph and Jon Hamm, takes a deep dive into the shady world of billionaire oil tycoons.

Thornton leads as crisis executive Tommy Norris, who attempts to bring his company to the top during a fueling boom. A release date for season three of Landman is currently unknown.

Dutton Ranch (2026-)

open image in gallery Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser play power couple Beth and Rip in 'Dutton Ranch' ( Paramount+ )

While the latest Yellowstone sequel, Dutton Ranch, was not officially created by Sheridan, it is based on original characters he created.

The series, which premiered in May, welcomes back Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser as power couple Beth Dutton and Rip Wheeler. The show follows their relocation to South Texas after a devastating fire destroys their Montana ranch.

Dutton Ranch broke Paramount+ streaming records, becoming the platform’s biggest original series launch yet.

Marshals (2026-)

open image in gallery Luke Grimes reprises his ‘Yellowstone’ character Kayce Dutton in 'Marshals' ( Sonja Flemming/CBS )

The Luke Grimes-led series, Marshals, is similarly built on Yellowstone characters originally established by Sheridan. This time, the spin-off focuses on Kayce (Grimes), the youngest Dutton son, and his transition to joining an elite unit of U.S. Marshals.

Combining his skills as a cowboy and Navy SEAL to bring range justice to Montana, Kayce and his colleagues must balance family, duty and the high psychological cost that comes with serving as the last line of defense in the region’s war on violence.

The Madison (2026-)

open image in gallery Michelle Pfeiffer stars in the standalone series 'The Madison' ( Emerson Miller/Paramount+ )

The Madison was initially conceived as a Yellowstone spin-off, but it has since been labeled a standalone series.

It features Michelle Pfeiffer as Stacy Clyburn, a grieving New Yorker who relocates her family to the Madison River valley of central Montana after an unexpected death. The popular series has already been renewed for a third season, even before season two has aired.

On the way

1944

Paramount announced 1944, a planned follow-up to the Yellowstone prequel 1923, in November 2023. The series, which is still in development, is said to follow the Dutton family and the impact of World War II.

Frisco King

Frisco King is a forthcoming spin-off of Tulsa King, starring Samuel L. Jackson as ex-con Russell Lee Washington Jr., who befriended Dwight in prison. Sent on a mission to eliminate Dwight in Tulsa, he is instead inspired to build his own criminal empire in Frisco, Texas.

The debut season wrapped filming in July and is anticipated to premiere in early 2027.

Ended

Yellowstone (2018-2025)

open image in gallery Kevin Costner led the first four seasons of ‘Yellowstone,’ before departing midway through the fifth ( Paramount )

Yellowstone, the flagship show that started it all, starred Costner as John Dutton, the patriarch of a family of homesteaders in Montana. Costner led the show for the first four seasons before ultimately quitting midway through its fifth and final season.

His exit prompted Sheridan to end the show prematurely. At the time, there were rumors that Costner had locked horns with Sheridan over scheduling conflicts. However, the TV mogul dispelled those rumors during a recent appearance on The Bill Simmons podcast, explaining that “[Costner] was only supposed to be in the first three seasons. That was in his contract. In my mind, that’s when his youngest son takes over [on the show], but the network was so scared of not having Kevin be a part of it.”

Sheridan said that Costner “was ready to go” as “he had other things he wanted to do,” including his ill-fated Western trilogy Horizon, but the Bodyguard actor remained on the show for another two seasons as it had become “such a behemoth.”

The Last Cowboy (2019-2023)

In 2019, Sheridan dipped his toe into the world of reality TV with The Last Cowboy. The documentary-style series chronicled the elite Western horse-riding competition of horse reining.

The contest saw eight men and women compete against one another as they guided their horses through a precise pattern of circles, spins and stops for the chance to win $1 million.

1883 (2021-2022)

open image in gallery Sam Elliott starred in '1883' as grieving cowboy Shea Brennan ( MTV Entertainment Group )

The first prequel to Yellowstone was 1883. Starring real-life couple Tim McGraw and Faith Hill as James and Margaret Dutton, the drama miniseries explored their journey, from fleeing poverty in Texas to settling down in Montana, where they built the Dutton Ranch.

1923 (2022-2025)

open image in gallery ‘1923’ starred Harrison Ford opposite Helen Mirren ( Paramount+ )

The arrival of 1923 came nearly a year after the conclusion of 1883. The second major prequel to Yellowstone followed Jacob Dutton (Harrison Ford), the older brother of James, as he and his wife, Cara (Helen Mirren), face challenges to protect their land and family amid Western expansion, Prohibition and the Great Depression.

News.title: Robinson demolishes Pakistan to cement importance to new regime
News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

News.title: Burnham blames Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation
News.content:
Andy Burnham has blamed Donald Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation in Britain.

Inflation jumped from 2.6pc in June to 2.9pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics, threatening to undermine Mr Burnham’s pledge to bring down the cost of living.

The Prime Minister said: “We can’t control though what is going on in the Middle East and the effect of the conflict there is now being felt in inflation here, and in other countries around the world.

“I realise these times are really hard but already people can see a month into office I have done things that will make a difference.”

July’s inflation figure was affected by a 13.5pc rise in the Ofgem price cap in response to the energy crisis unleashed by the Iran war. It means prices are now rising at their highest rate since March.

The latest figure shows the struggle that Mr Burnham faces to fulfil his promise to bring down living costs.

There are fears that inflation will climb higher in the coming months as the impact of the conflict filters through to the economy.

Speaking at an event in the North East, Mr Burnham added: “I want to lead a cost-of-living Government, and I’ve already taken steps as Prime Minister to show I will help people wherever I can. I can’t do everything, I think people know that.

“We’re in tough times, but where I can do something to make life that little bit better, I will do it.”

Since arriving in No 10, Mr Burnham has made tackling the cost of living a key policy focus.

The Prime Minister announced last month that he would remove VAT from electricity bills from October and reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares from next year.

However, average energy bills are expected to jump by around 4pc from October, according to energy analysts Cornwall Insight, wiping out any potential savings from Mr Burnham’s VAT cut.

The analysts said Ofgem’s price cap – which limits the average annual energy bill faced by a family home – would rise from £1,663 to £1,729.

Despite concerns about increasing gas and electricity bills, July’s rate of inflation was in line with economists’ expectations.

Money markets now expect policymakers at the Bank of England to hold interest rates at 3.75pc at their next meeting in September.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

New signings can be a slight risk to include in your very first starting XI. However, many teams got a lot of their business done early this year and there is always a thrill in the unknown of unearthing a potential new fantasy football star. Here are our top five to look out for this season:



Mamadou Sangaré (£3.1m)

Ever since the introduction of tackle bonuses, combative midfielders have found their place in the hearts of Telegraph Fantasy Football faithfuls. Brentford’s Malian international could prove to be the next Palhinha or Gomes, with a steady stream of bonuses expected alongside the odd attacking return.



Marco Palestra (£2.7m)

The exciting full-back has played the majority of minutes in pre-season under new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, showing a willingness to push high up the pitch. If the defensive and attacking returns come as expected, the 21-year-old could make a mockery of his cheap price-tag.



Gonzalo García (£3.7m)

No doubt influenced by his stint in the dugout at the Santiago Bernabéu, Arbeloa beat off stiff competition to land the former Real Madrid striker. At 6’ tall, the striker possesses the physical attributes, alongside the technical ability, to thrive in the Premier League. TFF managers will be targeting the GW6 to GW8 run, where the Cottagers play all three promoted clubs back-to-back, as a great entry point to transfer the Spaniard in.



Luka Vušković (£2.9m)

Brighton’s qualification for Europe was built on a solid defensive structure last season, and the ex-Tottenham centre-half has been brought in to fill the Van Hecke-sized hole in their back-line. The highly-regarded 19-year-old could be one of the bargains of the season if he lives up to his potential on the South Coast.



Tarik Muharemović (£2.7m)

TFF managers have a plethora of great value defensive assets to pick from this season, and the Bosnian could be the pick of the bunch. Having already demanded attention after scoring with an audacious bicycle-kick in pre-season, it won’t be a surprise to see the new Leeds no.5 in many final drafts.

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five key budget enablers
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.

Telegraph Fantasy Football managers need to make compromises to fit in fantasy heavyweights like Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Bruno Fernandes (6.5m). Picking some set-and-forget budget enablers who have either high point ceiling potential or will return a steady stream of points, is key to freeing up those funds.

Below are five players the Fantasy Football Hub experts have highlighted for consideration.





Brian Brobbey (£3.3m)

The Sunderland forward had a steady Premier League debut season, netting seven times and helping the Black Cats qualify for the Europa League. The Dutch international netted three times at the World Cup, improving his stock further, and will be looking to get off to a goal-scoring start against Ipswich and Fulham in GWs 1 and 2.



Enzo Le Fee (£3.3m)

Depending on the formation TFF managers are using, Brobbey’s midfield teammate at the same price may be the preferred route to target those opening fixtures. The 26-year-old accrued 12 attacking returns last season, and bumped up his overall score with an impressive 93 tackles.



Harry Wilson (£3.2m)

The midfielder swapped London for Yorkshire in the summer, as he looks to expand on a whopping 17 attacking returns from last season. Feeding the rejuvenated Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.9m), and adding goals from midfield for Leeds will be two primary objectives for the Welsh international, who could make a mockery of his mere marginal price increase.



James Trafford (£3.0m)

Another Leeds United summer acquisition, Daniel Farke fought off rival Premier League suitors to land the ex-Manchester City shot-stopper. Leeds United have a mixed bag in terms of opening fixture difficulty, but do have three home league games in the first five before the international break, and the new no.1 has an outside chance of getting the nod in the Carabao Cup games too, so there are points available should the Whites be able to shut out the opposition.



James Hill (£2.6m)

If looking to fit in more big-hitters, a sub £3m player can be extremely useful for team balance, and the Bournemouth defender looks assured of starting having played a pivotal role in getting the Cherries into Europe this season.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta changes Win the dog’s name after Premier League title triumph and Arsenal fans love it
Sports.content:
ARSENAL boss Mikel Arteta has delighted fans after renaming their dog Win to ‘Won’ following their Premier League title win.

The Spaniard brought the chocolate Labrador to the team’s London Colney base in 2023 in a bid to improve the club’s family atmosphere.



He also gave it the name ‘Win’ to ensure the players were always thinking of getting three points.

Three years after the pup’s arrival, Arsenal finally sealed Prem title glory – their first league crown in 22 years.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

And Arteta has decided to change the dog’s name to ‘Won’ after the team became champions.

He was interviewed by Men in Blazers and asked how Win had changed over the years.

Arteta replied: “So we change now – instead of ‘Win’ it’s ‘Won’. And now we’re going to put it – we want to win again.

The interviewer then asked: “Is it as simple as this: Get a dog, call it win. Nominative determination does the rest?”

Arteta laughed and said: “It’s that simple.”

Sports.title: Man Utd target Carlos Baleba is the perfect Casemiro successor who dreams of becoming the next Modric or Kroos
Sports.content:
CARLOS BALEBA is the Premier League-proven runner Manchester United need.

Saturday’s 4-2 defeat against AC Milan in Wroclaw shined a light on the lack of energy and depth in midfield.



United have made an opening offer of £65million for Brighton midfielder Baleba, who is eager to fly to Manchester and agree a five-year-deal.

Talks between the two clubs are in progress and United are hopeful of striking a deal for the 22-year-old Cameroon international, who has been a long-term target for the club.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

The Seagulls are open to selling Baleba for less than the £100m price tag quoted last summer.

United chiefs are clamping down hard on recruitment, bringing a brutal end to the wild spending days.

The club have also rejoiced in keeping their cards close to their chest this time around.

Baleba’s arrival would take United’s midfield spend to £150m this summer, meaning just £34m would separate United’s three midfield additions from City’s one marquee signing in Elliot Anderson.

Despite the hype around United’s midfield rebuild, rivals City look set to pull off an even larger overhaul, closing in on targets Ayyoub Bouaddi (£100m) and Enzo Fernandez (£120m).

United have splashed a combined £85m on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, with CEO Omar Berrada insisting market forces would not force their hand into panicked deals.

“His success has opened the door for midfielders like us to believe we can win the Ballon d’Or someday.”

Baleba’s journey is nothing short of remarkable so far. In 2022 he was still in Cameroon, uncertain about his future.

When he finally got his breakthrough move to Lille, tragedy struck, he lost his mother.

Baleba has fulfilled his promise to mum to build a house in Douala and remembers how she would encourage his dad – who played professionally as a striker in Cameroon and South Africa before coaching his son at the Cameroonian academy École de Football des Brasseries – to work him hard as a child.

Sports.title: Hull coach opens up on tragic death of 17-month-old daughter, Ten Hag’s £1,500 gift and taking on his beloved Man Utd
Sports.content:
OLD TRAFFORD season ticket holders never want Manchester United to lose.

But Hull City assistant Dean Holden will again put childhood loyalties aside in Saturday’s Premier League opener.



Holden is a lifelong Red Devils fan and has had an Stretford End season ticket for 34-years – but will be plotting United’s downfall in the rival dugout for Saturday’s Premier League opener.

United have always been central to life for Salford-born Holden, though keeping the newly-promoted Tigers in the top-flight is now his priority.



He previously managed against United when he was Charlton boss for a 2023 League Cup game and was also Bristol City’s No2 when they stunned Jose Mourinho’s United in the same competition in 2017.

Holden explains how he found out about the opening-day meeting, telling SunSport: “I was waiting at home all morning for the fixtures to come out and I had to take our youngest son Chase to school.

“As I got in the car my phone just started to blow up. My dad was ringing and Danielle was at home, my wife with the other kids.

“It was a great moment because it’s a big part of my life is that football club.

“My very first day in the job of being the Charlton manager was the Carabao Cup quarter-final draw when we played United.”

Holden played over 400 EFL matches as a defender for 10 different clubs, many of the years scuppered through injury, but the season ticket has been in his family since 1992.



Fixtures Results Table Arsenal 20:00 Regular Season Coventry Hull 12:30 Regular Season Man Utd Everton 15:00 Regular Season Palace Ipswich 15:00 Regular Season Sunderland Forest 15:00 Regular Season Leeds Brentford 17:30 Regular Season Spurs No results yet P W D L GD Pts 1 Arsenal 0 0 0 0 0 0 2 Villa 0 0 0 0 0 0 3 Bournemouth 0 0 0 0 0 0 4 Brentford 0 0 0 0 0 0 5 Brighton 0 0 0 0 0 0 6 Chelsea 0 0 0 0 0 0 7 Coventry 0 0 0 0 0 0 8 Palace 0 0 0 0 0 0

And his phone has been ringing off the hook with calls for tickets from friends about Hull’s first game back in the top-flight in nine years.

He joked: “I’ve just had people coming out of the woodwork asking for tickets and it’s a nightmare. It’s an absolute nightmare and I’m scrambling.”

Holden previously said United are “in his blood” and he was an Old Trafford ball-boy as a kid.

He told SunSport: “My dad was a steward at Old Trafford and he has taken me around to pretty much every side of that stadium over the years from being a young kid.



“So all my memories of being a kid, of going to games and queuing up overnight for tickets and going around the country watching them.”

When he took his Charlton side to Old Trafford for the last-eight tie almost four years ago, then-manager Erik ten Hag left him a gift after Marcus Rashford’s late double ended any hopes of a cup shock.

His friend later Googled the bottle of red wine gifted by Ten Hag—only to discover it was valued at a whopping £1,500.

He said: “We’ve still not opened that. So that’s going to be one for the kids in the future, hopefully. My kids also got one of Rashford’s signed shirts too.



“I learned a lot from Ten Hag and to get him behind closed doors without any cameras, he was really honest.

“He was extremely kind and generous with his time and his advice. I’m always trying to learn and find new ways of doing things, so he appreciated that.”

Despite the romantic opening-day storyline, Holden is hellbent on helping manager Sergej Jakirovic keep Hull in the top flight, reminding the squad to look at the long haul.

Holden and Jakirovic first met face-to-face in a heated touchline clash in the Turkish Super Lig during early 2025, while Holden was working at Adana Demirspor and Jakirovic was managing Kayserispor.



He said: “Sergei’s assistant recognised me during the Hull interview and I got the job. They appreciated I took over an already-relegated side and wanted someone who knew the Championship.

“Maybe squaring up to an opposition manager is the secret to success and hope he might give you a job in the future! It went in my favour in the end and the rest is history.

With promotion secured, Hull are finally free of EFL transfer restrictions ahead of the 2026–27 season.

The club had been serving a two-window fee limitation—reduced from three on appeal—over late payments to rival clubs.



Holden added: “We need to look at the bigger picture. The United game is the first game of the season, and it is not going to dictate our whole season.

“Sergej and his team deserve so much credit. To turn up in English football unannounced and to get promoted with a transfer embargo, is one of the most magical things that’s happened in the Championship in the last 20 years.”

The camaraderie between the two is obvious when Sergej wanders into the room mid-interview, cheekily trying to negotiate a guest appearance on Holden’s family YouTube channel, Holden It Together.

The YouTube show will cover Hull’s first season in the top-flight since 2017 and offers an insight into grief.

Holden and TV presenter wife Danielle tragically lost their daughter Cici, aged 17 months, after she contracted meningococcal septicaemia, while they were on holiday in Lanzarote in May 2012.



The family hopes their channel serves as a beacon for others facing loss—proof that even in the darkest moments, couples and families can work through grief together.

Holden explained: “When Cici passed we were on the canvas for a long time. We miss her every day.

“Now we hope that if you watch us in action at home in our real life, it’s a tale of hope and inspiration, showing how we can come through something so tragic and devastating.

“We’re trying to shine a light on just a real honest family who are trying to have a little bit of fun and not take life too seriously.

“It sounds a bit cliche, but if it can help one person, because there will be someone sat at home and struggling who maybe reads or listens to this and thinks, bloody hell, he’s in a tough industry himself, but he’s still prepared to talk.



“And I say to people all the time, ‘give me a shout on Instagram or anything’, I’m always up for talking about stuff like this.

“I’ll be honest, it helps me selfishly because I’m able to talk about Cici, it’s been a long time that we’ve not been with her and we miss her.”

The couple’s children Joey, Ellis, Mitzi and Chase, who wants to be a YouTuber, are all characters on the fun channel.

Joey and Ellis joined Holden on ‘lads’ holiday in Ibiza this summer, with Steven Gerrard and his wife Alex sorting them out a VIP table at Ocean Beach when it was sold out. Danielle flew out for the day.

Holden was hired as Gerrard’s assistant at Saudi Pro League club Al-Ettifaq in 2024 after delivering a “stinging attack” in his interview.



The current Hull coach replaced Ian Parker on the Anfield hero’s staff after impressing during an interview at London airport hotel.

Holden said: “He almost sees the game in slow motion. He is one of the greatest players this country has ever produced.

“Whether you are a United fan or not. He is one of the greatest. I got to spend that time inside his head. He’s incredible at handling pressure and his work ethic is second to none.”

Gerrard invited Holden to do a presentation as part of his interview process in early 2024, asking him to analyse a poor performance from Al-Ettifaq.

Holden said: “I just thought I’ll be honest with him, he comes from where I come from, he’s worked his way up from humble beginnings to megastardom.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It was a tough process but I delivered a stinging attack on his team’s performance and he appreciated my honesty and my take on football.”

Holden himself has dreams head coach return one day after stints with Oldham, Bristol City, Stoke City and Charlton. But first it is all steam ahead with Hull’s Prem season.

Sports.title: Who will win title? Will Max leave Red Bull? - Key questions as F1 returns
Sports.content:
Formula 1's summer break is over and the 2026 season restarts in the Netherlands this weekend as the championship run-in looms over the final months of the campaign.

We asked Sky Sports F1 pundit Karun Chandhok to run the rule over some of the key questions left to be answered on and off track this year and predict how things might pan out from here…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See what some of the Formula 1 drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

How many drivers still have a realistic title shot?

Kimi Antonelli's 50-point championship lead puts him firmly in the hunt, but fewer points cover Lewis Hamilton in second down to Lando Norris, the winner of the last race in Hungary, in fifth. With two Sprints and up to 12 Grands Prix to go, there are potentially as many as 316 points left to play for between now and December.

Karun says: "I think, realistically, this is Antonelli's championship to lose. Nobody has come back from this big a points deficit since we went to this scoring system in 2010. Kimi is driving well, he has got a lot of confidence in the car and the way it's working for him.

"The only Achilles' heel seems to be Mercedes' reliability. That could be a challenge, but they are going to keep improving that. So realistically, I think it is his championship to lose, which is an extraordinary achievement in just his second year in F1.

"The only thing I would say is, with the way the upgrades and updates are going, it will be interesting to see what Ferrari can do, and also whether any of Mercedes' upgrades help George Russell out, because it does feel like he has had obviously more bad luck but also a pace disadvantage this year.

"I think it is only Lewis or maybe George who could challenge him, but it's more his to lose."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the Formula 1 season set to resume after the summer break, we look back at how Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has built a 50-point lead in the driver standings.

Which team is the one to watch for development?

In-season car development is always crucial in Formula 1 but the stakes have been raised this year with teams still in the early stages of understanding how to unlock the best performance from the all-new 2026 aerodynamic rules and engines. The first half of the season saw teams make big jumps in performance at races they brought update packages, and others did not, with that trend expected to continue after the summer break.

Karun says: "I'm interested to see what McLaren do. Clearly the car was very good in Budapest and that bodes well for the Dutch Grand Prix because whoever is good in Budapest should have a good car for Zandvoort.

"And they've got more bits coming this weekend on the rear end of the car as well, which is the second half of the update.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

"The big one to keep an eye out for is Red Bull, because they have been a bit more inconsistent and there's a bit of a battle on for them to play catch-up.

"If you look at it across the season, they have had the fourth-fastest car, which is not ideal in terms of trying to keep Max happy and at the team.

"So, Red Bull are the ones I'm most interested in watching out for to see if they can dig themselves out of this hole in terms of inconsistencies."

Where will Max Verstappen end up driving for 2027?

The big question on which the volatility of the driver market hinges. Max Verstappen is contracted to Red Bull until the end of 2028 but a position outside the top two of the Drivers' Championship at the summer break - he sits in sixth place - means he is free to activate a break clause in the deal for the end of this year, should he wish. The answer to the question of whether he will or not remains unknown with Verstappen thought to have until October to tell Red Bull should he want to leave. Immediate alternative options for him for 2027, however, should he want to continue in F1 remain uncertain despite links to McLaren and Mercedes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Max Verstappen's troublesome 2026 season, with the Red Bull driver having suffered multiple issues.

Karun says: "I have no idea when Max will end up driving in 2027 but I think realistically, I don't think he knows yet either.

"I think he is waiting to see where the Red Bull goes and really what other options there are."

Will Fernando Alonso race on or retire from F1 for 2027?

Fernando Alonso said he would use the summer break to decide on whether he will extend his F1 career into a record-extending 24th campaign next season. The Spaniard, who turned 45 in July and became a father for the first time earlier this year, has downplayed suggestions his decision completely rests on how competitive he expects Aston Martin to be in 2027, saying that it will also be influenced on how he feels about the sport's current rules.

Karun says: "I think if Aston can demonstrate that they are going to make progress and Honda can demonstrate that they are making progress and they can give Alonso a car that at least gets him into Q3 and gives him something to fight for in 2027, then he will stick around.

"He is not going to stick around to be someone who gets knocked out in Q1 all the time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso said Aston Martin’s new upgrades delivered improvements in Hungary.

How high will Aston Martin get up the grid?

The clear underperformer of the season's first half after all manner of issues with their 2026 chassis and Honda engine left them at the back of the grid, Aston Martin delivered what they hope will provide the first of many steps forward with their first car upgrade last time out in Hungary. Further revisions to Adrian Newey's AMR26 and the first long-awaited engine upgrade, which is set to arrive at Zandvoort, offer the potential for further progress heading towards 2027.

Karun says: "Aston Martin have got to get themselves in a position where they need to end this year at least occasionally getting into Q3 because that then lays the foundation for 2027 and beyond.

"The engine upgrades will be critical for that. If you look at their straight-line speed at Spa, it was shocking. They brought the updated chassis to Budapest and that seemed to give them some performance advantage, a decent step.

"So really with the engine advantage, they might occasionally sneak themselves into Q3, which would be good progress but more importantly, a good foundation."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the last Formula One race coming up at Zandvoort, look back at some of the most dramatic moments throughout the years at the Dutch Grand Prix.

How many drivers will win races over the remaining rounds?

F1 broke for summer on a run of five different winners in as many races with both Mercedes drivers, both Ferrari drivers and McLaren's Lando Norris standing on the top step of the podium during that run.

Karun says: "I think there is a chance we could see both Ferrari drivers, McLaren drivers and Mercedes drivers winning races, and Max.

"If Red Bull do upgrade well and bring good bits and pieces, then we could see Max winning. He wasn't that far off in Austria, and the car steadily made progress. They need a couple of jumps and they could do it."

What will Sepang be like on F1's return and who might the track favour?

For the first time in nine years, F1 will race at the much-loved Sepang International Circuit in October after Malaysia agreed to host the Bahrain Grand Prix. Sepang built a reputation as both a driver and fan favourite across its 18 years on the calendar, with the track featuring challenging corner combinations and providing good racing.

Karun says: "I love Sepang. I first raced there in 2001, which was my first year of international racing. I've been back in lots of different categories and have always absolutely loved the circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule to host the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season.

"I think it is a really interesting, challenging layout, good for racing. I'm delighted to see everyone going back there, albeit temporarily.

"I think we are going to see a fantastic race. For this year's cars, there are plenty of opportunities to harvest and recharge the batteries and energy around chunks of the lap, so it should be a pretty good race all round.

"It is going to be hot, so anyone who can keep the tyre temperatures under control will be in good shape."

Who will win the 2026 championships?

Antonelli's half-century lead at mid-season makes him the clear bookmakers' favourite ahead of Lewis Hamilton and George Russell, who was most people's tips for the title at the start of the year.

Mercedes would likely have been away and clear already and not just 72 points ahead of Ferrari had they not suffered from reliability problems. Nonetheless, Ferrari outscored them in each of the three races before the summer break and, with reliability on their side, aren't to be ruled out yet. McLaren were 78 points back on Red Bull with 12 races to go in 2024 and ended up as champions.

Karun says: "I think this is Antonelli's drivers' title to lose, and Mercedes' Constructors' Championship to lose."

Sports.title: England skittle Pakistan at Headingley on Root's return as Test captain
Sports.content:
Joe Root's second spell as England Test captain began with his side skittling Pakistan for 171 at Headingley as Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each bagged five-wicket hauls around a lengthy rain delay and a brief fightback from the tourists.

Root is back in charge following Ben Stokes' shock international retirement in June and charged with turning around the team's fortunes after seven defeats and just one win in their last 10 games, across fixtures against India, Australia and New Zealand.

Bar wet weather preventing any play from 11.50pm-1.45pm, and Abdullah Shafique (61) and Imam-ul-Haq (42) putting on a stand of 91 from 6-2, this was an excellent day for Root, with Pakistan rolled in 48.1 overs before the hosts closed on 112-2 in reply, trailing by 59.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson's fifth Test five-for included a beauty to bowl Pakistan's top-scorer Abdullah Shafique for 61

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue completed his five-for and ended the Pakistan innings in one foul swoop by bowling Mohammad Abbas

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, first Test, Headingley Pakistan 171 all out in 48.1 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Abdullah Shafique (61), Imam-ul-Haq (42); Salman Ali Agha (21); Josh Tongue (5-46), Ollie Robinson (5-51) England 112-2 after 25 overs in first innings (trail by 59 runs): Joe Root (37no), Emilio Gay (33), Jordan Cox (23no), Ben Duckett (15); Mohammad Abbas (1-34), Mohammad Ali (1-38)

England lost Ben Duckett (15) lbw and Emilio Gay (33) caught at slip, to Mohammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali respectively, leaving Jordan Cox (23no) - into the side at No 3 in place of the injured Jacob Bethell - and Root (37no) to usher the side to the 7.30pm stumps with an unbroken stand of 64.

The day had been extended after the earlier rain, which could return in droves on day two.

Root - whose first stint in charge from 2017-2022 preceded the fabulously entertaining but ultimately flawed Bazball era - had no hesitation in bowling after winning the toss under leaden skies on his home ground and that decision reaped immediate rewards.

Robinson (5-51) inflicted a platinum duck on Azan Awais, trapping the opener lbw from around the wicket as a wicket fell to the first ball of a Test match in England for the first time in 19 years, and then pinned Shan Masood (5) leg before from over the wicket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson trapped Azan Awais lbw for a duck from the first ball of the Headingley Test

Pakistan battled to 23-2 from 9.4 overs before the rain arrived, during which time England burned two reviews looking for further breakthroughs, and then progressed to 97-3 once play resumed, only for Tongue (5-46) nicking off Imam to trigger a collapse.

The away side lost their final eight wickets for 74 and last five for 21, with the clatter including Robinson bowling Shafique with a beauty that jagged in prodigiously and the same bowler pinning Saud Shakeel (5) lbw after the batter took two long to request a review that would have saved him - the ball was set to soar over leg stump.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pakistan's Saud Shakeel was left to rue taking too long to review an lbw dismissal - with Robinson's delivery set to bounce over the stumps

Tongue's hat-trick hopes dashed as Pakistan razed

Tongue was on a hat-trick as the players emerged after tea having bowled stand-in Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha (21) - who is deputising for Babar Azam (hand) - through the gate and then trapped Ali Usman (0) lbw before the break.

Pakistan No 9 Khurram Shahzad (14) denied Tongue that magic moment, with a crunching cover-driven four, but Tongue snared a fourth Test five-for by going on to remove Mohammad Rizwan (12) lbw and obliterate the off stump of Abbas (2).

Robinson's fifth five-for in the format, and second of the summer, could have come two balls earlier than it did, only for Gus Atkinson to spill Khurram's hack to mid-on, yet Atkinson made no mistake shortly after when Khurram sliced down the ground once again.

This is the skilful Robinson's first Test since the series opener against New Zealand at Lord's, a game in which he bagged a triple-wicket maiden, seven wickets all told and was named Player of the Match, and he bowled with immense accuracy and control here, too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Stuart Broad looks at why Robinson has previously been over-looked for England selection and what his key assets are

The same could not be said of Jofra Archer (0-26 from nine overs), who struggled with his line and length at times - conceding 12 runs off his fourth over - and looked very much like a man who has had a diet of white-ball cricket over the last few months.

Archer, who was hooked after two overs after sharing the new ball with Robinson, should be better for the runout.

Shafique had entered this Test off the back of a fifty in the sole warm-up against a County Select XI last week and an unbeaten 160 in the Test win in the West Indies earlier this month.

He looked well attuned to red-ball cricket - once he had survived a one-sided early tussle with Tongue, that is - as he compiled a sixth Test fifty, from 82 deliveries, before falling to Robinson's jaffa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay were dismissed in quick succession during the first day of the first Test against Pakistan

England opener Gay had bagged a pair playing for the County XI against Pakistan in that aforementioned tune-up fixture in Beckenham but he got off the mark second ball in Leeds with a nerve-settling single and then stroked and clipped a number of pleasing boundaries before prodding to slip.

The home side could face a long wait before they bat again as Thursday's forecast is rotten but whenever play does resume, it will do so with England in a strong position, with Abbas' fellow Pakistan seamers Khurram and Ali unable to match his precision as they leaked runs and Root now ominously settled.

Tongue: England in a great position

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Josh Tongue reflects on a positive first day of the Test match against Pakistan

England fast bowler Josh Tongue (5-46), talking to Sky Sports:

"We're in a great position now but that first hour tomorrow morning - it might do a bit more at 11am.

"If we focus on that first hour, we can get a good lead.

"As a bowling unit, we were very good and Robinson was excellent. It was similar to his performance at Lord's against New Zealand.

"He's an exceptional bowler when he hits his lines and lengths and he showed that today."

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's York tips: Ebor Festival day two picks
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing’s Kevin Blake reveals a trio of picks as York's Ebor Festival rolls on into day two on Thursday.

The Ebor Festival at York rolls on into day two on Thursday and while the main events will provide world-class action for us to enjoy, it is the supporting card that might well offer the best betting opportunities.

The Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap (3:00) is yet another brutally-tough handicap puzzle to solve, but William Haggas may have the answer in the shape of BULLET POINT. The five-year-old won this race last year off a mark of 100, enjoying a smooth trip around from a good draw and winning with some authority.

However, his career hasn't continued on the upward curve as might have been expected since then, with a trip down to Australia ending in disappointment followed by a six-month absence. Since his return, it wouldn't be at all surprising if his connections have been working backwards from this race.

He shaped with subtle promise in two runs in valuable handicaps earlier this season and then returned from another 12 weeks off to run a fine race in defeat at the Shergar Cup, finding just one that had got loose on the lead too good for him. He gets to run off the same mark of 101 here and while the draw hasn't been quite so good to him this year as it was last year, he still looks to have leading prospects.

The next contest of interest is the Mews Hotel Ossett EBF Stallions Nursery (4:45). Three weeks ago, this column put up the Hugo Palmer-trained MIA FANTASIA in a valuable nursery at Glorious Goodwood. To say he had a troubled passage would be underselling it! He got next to no luck in running and shaped much better than the bare result.

The case that made for him that day remains relevant, with him having overcome his inexperience to win in good style at Carlisle on debut before not quite being sharp enough to be as competitive in what has proven to be a smart novice contest at Ascot that was won by the subsequent Vintage Stakes winner Dr Rascal. A mark of 79 seems very fair indeed and he is sure to have benefited from the experience he gained at Goodwood. He looks likely to run a big race.

The final race of interest on the day is another very tough handicap, the British EBF Fillies' Handicap (5:20). Again, cases can be made for so many of these, but I'm going to venture down towards the bottom end of the weights and side with the Ed Walker-trained SECRET HISTORY.

The three-year-old has already won three times this year, with her most notable victory coming in a valuable seven-furlong handicap at Newmarket in July. Raised 4lb for that, her connections took a chance in dropping her to six furlongs to contest a valuable fillies' handicap at Glorious Goodwood and while she ran well to finish third, she shaped as though the test was sharper than ideal for her. Returning to this trip will be a big help to her and she looks to have very strong prospects.

Sports.title: Masters, Webb criticise FIFA over Balogun red card controversy
Sports.content:
Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban.

Richard Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game.

Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced.

However, US president Donald Trump then called FIFA president Gianni Infantino to complain, which led to the decision being overturned and Balogun was allowed to play against Belgium in the last 16.

Webb said: "I was really troubled by it. I don't know the ins and outs of the process, but what we know is: a red card was shown. You can form an opinion about the validity of the red card, I can understand why it was given.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Geraint Hughes explains what could happen next in Folarin Balogun's red card controversy, despite Belgium beating the USA in the World Cup

"We know that there was pressure placed by a politician onto FIFA, because that was admitted. We know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament, and suspended, through a process which seemingly didn't exist before the tournament started.

"Decisions that had been taken previously were viewed as correct or incorrect, based on your judgement. Far too often now, decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media.

"They try to draw inferences around decisions they don't agree with and what the motivation is behind that decision. But that is borne out of no fact, no evidence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player US President Donald Trump admits he asked FIFA to review Folarin Balogun's suspension for the Round of 16 match against Belgium, following his red card against Bosnia & Herzegovina

"And when you get that situation, it opens up the space for people to think 'this sort of thing is happening all the time behind the scenes' - and it's not."

Masters, who on Tuesday called on FIFA to sack Infantino, agrees.

He said: "We should be looking back on the World Cup, the football that was played, Spain being the best team, and England's agonising semi-final defeat. But we're not, we are talking about other issues, and that's a huge shame.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chief Refereeing Officer for Professional Game Referees, Howard Webb, discussed the changes to VAR that will be in place for the 2026/27 Premier League season

"The Balogun issue stands alone in that isolated incident which is very difficult to comprehend when you look at it. I think it is, again, a self-inflicted moment (by FIFA).

"Why do FIFA not have a red card review process like the one that exists in many other leagues, including the Premier League, where if there has been a miscarriage of justice - not that I'm saying Balogun's red card was a miscarriage of justice - but it can be dealt with on that basis, rather than use a system which is only about the length of suspension which there is no option to overturn?

"That created controversy unnecessarily in my view."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player CEO of the Premier League Richard Masters discusses Gianni Infantino and Manchester City's alleged breaches of the league's financial rules. Man City deny all their charges

Masters went on to say that he hopes the Balogun controversy will not undermine confidence in referees and the disciplinary process in the Premier League, insisting the competition is completely honest and legitimate.

"Coming back to the issue of do people do believe their eyes, I do scroll through social media every now and then and I do bump into some of the stuff that some people are saying and thinking out there," he added.

"But I do believe that fans, when they turn up and we have 99 per cent sold out, and they watch what's going on on the pitch, it's everything that it should be. It's just the same. It's English football, everyone's trying their best, referees are trying their best, there's lots of controversy, but it is what it says it is."

Sports.title: Jaissle: Club aligned on Newcastle squad needing adjustments
Sports.content:
Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle says the club are aligned on the need for "adjustments" to the squad in the final few weeks of the summer transfer window.

It has been another turbulent summer for the Magpies, losing key players like Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon as well as Eddie Howe's departure.

The club has focused on bringing in young talent to replace their outgoing stars, with new boss Jaissle also recently landing one of his former players, Amar Dedic, from Benfica. "We will count on him," he said.

And when asked how many more he might like through the door, the German was non-committal, telling Sky Sports News: "I would love to answer that with a clear number, but it's depending also if players are leaving as well.

"For sure, there will be adjustments made, the needs are clear. The management knows about the needs and we are all aligned.

"We will use the remaining time [in the transfer window] in the best possible way, but also we trust the players who are already here."

Newcastle United

Liverpool Sunday 23rd August 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Jaissle does not seem overawed by the task at hand - including the rebuilding of a club who see themselves as top four contenders.

"I tried to not overthink beforehand," he explained. "I was aware of the challenge... and among such a journey there will always be stones among the path, but we need to get rid of them. We need to see the opportunities, the chance in all these things.

"This is something we mentioned already, and I feel that the players are committed towards these challenges in the transition period right now. I'm really optimistic for the future."

Four of Newcastle's seven summer signings are under the age of 21 - Sean Steur from Ajax is only 18 - and Jaissle has asked for time for them to adapt to the rigours of the Premier League.

Selected Newcastle transfers this summer IN:

Bazoumana Toure - Hoffenheim, £42m

Aladji Bamba - Monaco, £35.5m

Amar Dedic - Benfica, £29.5m

Lukas Hornicek - Braga, £25.7m

Sean Steur - Ajax, £23m

Ewen Jaouen - Reims, £18.5m

Amar Dedic - Benfica, £29.5m



OUT:

Sandro Tonali - Tottenham, £100m

Bruno Guimaraes - Arsenal, £75m

Anthony Gordon - Barcelona, £69.3m

Matt Targett - Hull, free

Kieran Trippier - Wolves, free

"You know that usually you need to have the adaptation time, therefore I said that you need to be patient with them and give them the time. It's always a process," he said.

"We should not give them too much pressure in the beginning. That's a goal from the club to work with young talents, to develop them and this is nice to see because that's a clear identity of the club.

"That's also the reason why I'm here because I'm used to working with young talents in my time in Salzburg and I also used to work with stars in Saudi Arabia, so it's a great fit and you can build on something."

Fans will be able to find out more about Jaissle and his new squad when Newcastle host Liverpool on Super Sunday, live on Sky Sports - something of a baptism of fire for the 38-year-old who will have been at the club for three-and-a-half weeks when he steps out at St James' Park.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the pre-season friendly match between Newcastle United and Valencia. Credit: Newcastle United

Reflecting on his time at the club so far, Jaissle added: "You are aware, like I am, that we need to fix things in a short amount of time.

"The timing was not ideal, but in football you cannot always have the perfect timing, so we need to do the best out of it.

"In a short amount of time, we need to be efficient, we need to implement the philosophy as much as possible, how the lads should enter the pitch and deliver the messages.

"They are doing an amazing job so far. They are really committed, they learn fast, but it will be a process.

"We are for sure not 100 per cent against Liverpool, but with the fans in the back, with the support from the stands, we can do special things here at St James' Park. I could feel that already in the friendly matches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matthias Jaissle gives his first interview as Newcastle head coach and discusses his plans on where he wants to take the club

The match will also be a meeting of two former clubs of Kevin Keegan - the Newcastle and Liverpool legend who passed away over the summer. There are plans for a series of tributes to the former forward before the game.

Jaissle added: "With the tributes, it's already a special game. It will be an outstanding atmosphere. I'm getting goosebumps just thinking about it so I can't wait."

Sports.title: 'Exceptional' Robinson hailed as he and Tongue cut match ball in half
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson was branded 'exceptional' by team-mate Josh Tongue after both pace bowlers bagged five-wicket hauls as England bowled Pakistan out for 171 runs on day one of the first Test match at Headingley.

After Tongue snared Mohammad Abbas to wrap up Pakistan's first innings, he and Robinson walked off the field holding hands, discussing who between them would take the match ball home.

Instead, they opted to split the ball in half, employing the help of the grounds staff to cut the ball through its seam.

"It's not often you get half a ball," Robinson told the ECB. "So it's something we'll remember forever. It's quite unique."

Robinson kickstarted proceedings in incredible fashion, pinning Azan Awais with the first ball of the Test match, before also snaring Shan Masood (5) lbw before rain stopped play.

He followed up by dismissing Abdullah Shafique (61), Saud Shakeel (5), and later got Khurram Shazad (14), to take the fifth five-fer of his Test career.

It followed his incredible seven-wicket haul at Lord's against New Zealand in June, his last Test appearance.

"Ollie Robinson was excellent," Tongue said. "As a bowling unit, we were very good. I'm glad that we bowled them out.

"It was similar to his performance at Lord's.

"He's an exceptional bowler when he hits his lines and lengths and he showed that today."

Broad: Robinson's bowling attributes are excellent

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson took a wicket with the very first ball of the Test match

Robinson missed both of England's second and third Test defeats against New Zealand earlier this summer, and prior to that, had not played for England for over two years, after falling out of favour with selectors, due to injuries and fitness issues.

After taking his first two wickets on Wednesday afternoon, Sky Sports Cricket analyst Stuart Broad commended Robinson on his bowling abilities.

"He's an excellent bowler, and certainly when conditions suit him, he's someone who is a great exponent of movement and can hold an area for a long period of time," Broad told Sky Sports Cricket.

Broad believes England will benefit from Robinson's talents over the coming years, with Root's side set to tour South Africa in the winter, before welcoming Australia for the 2027 Ashes.

"The advantage for England and Robinson over the next year is that they'll go to South Africa, where he'll be a fine bowler," Broad said.

"He's got brilliant attributes: he makes the ball bounce and hits consistent areas.

"Then you're into an Ashes series, we don't know what the pitches will be like, but you know that if you get a pitch with a bit of movement, Robinson is your best bowler for extracting that movement.

"Then he'll be around 33 the next time the English summer comes around, and England have a choice of rebuilding a new bowling attack going forward, or they want to keep dipping Ollie Robinson in and out for pitches that suit him.

"There's no doubt that you get him on Lord's or a nipper with a brand new ball, he's our best bowler in those conditions."

"Tongue is an awkward bowler to deal with," Dinesh Karthik told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast. "He's been bowling at his best in the last six to eight months. He has shown his ability to get good batters out when they're set, which is a good skill to have.
